Autonomous & Adaptable

Your Autonomous Mobile Network Testing Platform

Designed for continuous testing, monitoring, and diagnostics of 5G and LTE networks. Powered by Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 and equipped with Quectel modem, the Probe performs scheduled service-quality tests, collects radio parameters, and presents measurement results in real time.

Features & Benefits in Detail

5G & LTE Network Testing

Test 5G and LTE from one device

Perform tests and collect radio information in both 5G and LTE networks. RAT Lock and Band Lock functions allow the operator to isolate selected technologies and frequency bands during measurements.

Autonomous Operation

Runs scheduled tests with nobody on site

Define measurement scenarios and allow the probe to execute them independently. The device can perform recurring tests without a permanently connected workstation or continuous operator supervision.

Flexible Deployment

Installs with a single cable

Power the device through Power over Ethernet or a 12 V DC source. The available industrial interfaces support deployment in technical installations and integration with external equipment.

Remote and Local Access

Check results from anywhere, even on a phone

Manage the probe remotely through the mobile network or connect locally using its Wi-Fi hotspot. Measurement results, radio parameters, and device settings are available through a standard web browser.

Optional Four-SIM Flexibility

Compare up to four operators without swapping SIMs

The integrated SIM switch supports up to four independent SIM cards. Test multiple operators, subscriptions, APNs, or service configurations without manually replacing the SIM card.

Industrial System Integration

Connects to the industrial equipment you already run

Use isolated RS232, RS485, CAN, and ADC interfaces to connect the probe with industrial equipment, controllers, sensors, or external monitoring systems.

How It Works

1
Mount & Connect

Install the Probe at a remote or unmanned site. Connect via PoE (RJ45) or 12 V DC — a single cable delivers both power and data. Insert up to four SIM cards.

2
Define Measurement Schedules

Use N-Analytics Command Center to configure test scripts with drag-and-drop blocks, loops and validation. Published scripts launch on individual probes or entire groups.

3
Analyse Results in Real Time

Measurement results, radio parameters, and device status are presented in real time through the web-based interface. Geolocated coverage mapping combines results with location data.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the RFB Probe MKII 5G?+
An autonomous probe for continuous testing, monitoring and diagnostics of 5G and LTE networks. It runs scheduled service-quality tests, collects radio parameters and presents results in real time. It is built on a Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 with a Quectel RM520N-GL modem.
Which networks and bands does it support?+
5G NR in SA and NSA mode, LTE FDD (B1–B29, B32, B66, B71), LTE TDD (B34/38/39/40/41/42/43/48) and LTE LAA (B46). 5G NR NSA bands include n1/2/3/5/7/8/12/14/20/25/28/30/38/40/41/48/66/71/77/78/79; the modem is mmWave ready.
Can the probe test the network with nobody on site?+
Yes. You define measurement scenarios once and the probe runs them on its own, including recurring test schedules, without a permanently connected laptop or an operator watching.
Which tests can it run?+
Download, Upload, Latency, Delay and Voice Call test scripts. Advanced modem control adds RAT Lock and Band Lock, and results can be shown on a geolocated coverage map generated by the device.
Can I compare several mobile operators with one probe?+
Yes. The integrated SIM switch holds up to four independent SIM cards, so you can test different operators, subscriptions, APNs or service configurations without swapping cards by hand.
How is the probe powered and installed?+
With one cable: Power over Ethernet through the RJ45 port, or an external 12 V DC supply. It fits technical installations and remote or unmanned sites.
How do I see the results?+
Remotely over the mobile network through the active SIM, or locally through the probe's built-in Wi-Fi hotspot. Results, radio parameters and settings open in a standard web browser.
Can it connect to industrial equipment?+
Yes. Isolated RS232, RS485, CAN and ADC interfaces connect the probe to controllers, sensors and external monitoring systems.
What temperatures can it work in?+
Optimal operating range is -35 °C to +75 °C; extended range is -40 °C to +85 °C.
What is the difference between N-Analytics Station and N-Analytics Portal?+
N-Analytics Station comes free with every probe and gives web access to the results and settings of that one probe. N-Analytics Portal is a 12-month subscription for whole fleets: Fleet Manager, KPI alarms, scripted automation and outdoor and indoor analytics.
What is the difference between Probe MKII 5G and Probe MKII LTE450?+
The 5G model tests 5G NR and LTE, holds four SIM cards and has industrial interfaces. The LTE450 model is built for 450 MHz specialist and critical networks, runs on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Quectel EG950A modem and is powered over USB-C.
Where is the probe typically used?+
Mobile network optimisation, site survey and planning, deployment and acceptance testing, multi-network comparison, troubleshooting, private 5G and LTE networks in factories, warehouses and campuses, remote site monitoring and industrial system integration.
Can I order three or more probes online?+
Online orders cover one or two units of a product. From three units of one position, or for a custom setup, our sales team prepares an individual quote. A bundle counts as one unit.
